title: Burst consolidator and field sanitizer for OTLP->Tracing sinks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During peak ingest bursts our tracing pipeline forwards very large batches to downstream Jaeger/Tempo clusters which causes spikes in CPU, long tail latencies, and occasional dropped connections. In addition, some high-cardinality span attributes contain customer-identifiable fields (emails, file paths) that must be scrubbed before long-term retention.

Goal: Build a lightweight in-ingest proxy stage (Burst Consolidator) that detects short-term burst windows, coalesces spans for the same trace into compact envelopes, and applies deterministic field-sanitization rules before exporting to tracing backends. This should reduce downstream load, provide a clear privacy boundary, and enable a configurable export-window policy (flush sizes and time windows).

Scope:
- OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP ingest paths only (not SDK instrumentation).
- Export targets: Jaeger collector HTTP and Tempo OTLP (gRPC).
- Sanitization rules: regex-based PII masking for email, token-like strings; path trimming for filesystem paths; length clipping for high-cardinality tags. Rules must be configurable per-tenant.
- Export behaviour: Size-based gating and export-windowing; when envelope size exceeds threshold, split into bounded sub-envelopes preserving trace continuity. Provide metrics for envelopes created, spans dropped, and sanitize rate.

Non-goals: Full schema translation (we will not convert span model semantics), persistent storage of raw spans, or SDK-level instrumentation changes.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The consolidator reduces median downstream export batch count by >=30% on synthetic burst workload while keeping end-to-end 95th percentile export latency increase <= 15%.
AC2: Sanitization rules are configurable via tenant config and documented; sample tenant with PII fields shows no plaintext emails after processing.
AC3: System exposes Prometheus metrics: consolidator_envelopes_created, consolidator_spans_sanitized_total, consolidator_spans_dropped_total, consolidator_export_latency_seconds (histogram).
AC4: End-to-end tests (integration harness) exercising OTLP ingest -> consolidator -> Jaeger/Tempo show no data-loss for non-malformed spans and trace continuity is preserved.
AC5: Security review completed and approved (security_review_required = true).
tasks: Design consolidator control-plane: tenant config, thresholds, and runtime toggles (PM review)
Implement OTLP ingest interceptor that performs envelope grouping and streaming serialization
Implement field sanitizer with pluggable rules and safe defaults
Add adaptive split logic for oversized envelopes and ensure ordered sub-envelope exports
Integrate exporter adapters for Jaeger HTTP and Tempo OTLP with backpressure-aware writes
Add metrics, tracing, and dashboards for envelope/traffic characteristics
Write integration tests and load harness (k6 + local Jaeger) to validate behaviour
Prepare rollout plan: feature-flagged canary then tenant ramp

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Drop high-cardinality tags vs sanitize+clip — chose sanitize+clip to avoid losing correlation signals. 2) Wait-and-batch windowing introduces slight latency vs immediate passthrough; configured windows default to 50ms for low-latency tenants and 200ms for throughput-optimized tenants.
Performance target: per-span processing CPU < 0.5 microseconds in hot path for no-sanitize case; with sanitization expected overhead ~0.8-1.5 microseconds depending on rule complexity.
Rollback plan: feature flag off toggles in-memory consolidator; exporter drains current envelopes with a short grace period (configurable). Monitor consolidator_spans_dropped_total during rollback.
